clue.text: Financial arrangements for tales of the riverside

definitions.meaning: facilities a customer holds with a high-street lender for deposits and payments
stories told about a river's edge, a bank being the sloping ground beside a river

explanation.surface: A whimsical claim that money matters are really stories set beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a riverside is a bank, and accounts are tales or reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Customers hold these with a lender to keep money and make payments, so they are financial arrangements; read literally, they are stories about a river's edge.

clue.text: Characters who might help a bat if lost

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Some letters could aid a flying mammal that has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges HELP A BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Characters are letters, and the full set of letters is a script's characters.

clue.text: Recoil from such a thrill

definitions.meaning: the jolt of a gun when fired
a buzz or excitement, as in getting one from something

explanation.walkthrough: A gun's backward jolt and the excitement of 'getting one' from something share the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun jolts back when fired, its recoil; a buzz of excitement is also a kick.

clue.text: The secret of self-assurance

definitions.meaning: a private matter told in trust

explanation.walkthrough: One reading is a private matter told in trust, the other is belief in oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter shared in trust is a private secret; believing in your own ability is self-assurance.

clue.text: Clothes company

definitions.meaning: a set of garments worn together

explanation.definitionFit: A set of garments worn together is clothing; a business firm or group is also called one.

clue.text: Any live acts seen in a childish way

indicators.note: acts means performs on, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Every live performance is judged to be infantile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acts' rearranges ANY and LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting naively means acting innocently and without experience, like a child.

clue.text: Posed before one's group got revenge?

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat means posed
I'S is one's, with I as the Roman numeral one
a faction is a group within a party

explanation.surface: A model sat for a portrait, then had their clique take vengeance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got revenge' hints at the old phrase demanding satisfaction, as in a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand satisfaction was to seek redress for an insult, as in a duel; so it means revenge.

clue.text: Revolutionary worker wearing beret for sleep

indicators.note: wearing means having something put on, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a beret is a kind of cap

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word for the worker is read backwards

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A radical labourer in a beret takes a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads as a political label for the worker but signals turning the word round; 'wearing' means the beret sits on the outside, as a hat would.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short sleep, a brief doze.

clue.text: A politician on the left providing illumination

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is the usual crossword politician

explanation.surface: A left-wing member of parliament shedding light on some issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the left' places the L at the front, before A and MP; the surface wants 'on the left' to describe the politician's leanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A light fitting is a source of illumination, so the word stands for the brightness it gives by metonymy.

clue.text: Hamper politician on the right with authoritarian following

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a politician of the British right
strict means rigidly authoritarian, enforcing rules firmly

explanation.surface: A complaint that a right-wing politician with a hard-line following holds things back.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper is to restrict or hold back movement, which is what squeezing something tight does.

clue.text: Where one might be coming down bare?

definitions.text: Where one might be coming down bare?

parts.words: Where one might be coming down bare?
parts.note: reads as a place for undressing, but describes a runway where an aircraft descends

explanation.walkthrough: 'coming down' is an aircraft landing and 'bare' hints at a strip, as in undressing; the place is a simple runway.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft touch down on a basic runway, so it is where one comes down to land.

clue.text: Former queen with answer started to lose temper

parts.note: Queen Anne reigned over Britain from 1702 to 1714

indicators.note: started picks out how the word lose begins, just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A past monarch, faced with a reply, began to fly into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose temper' reads as one phrase about anger, but 'temper' is the definition in its metalworking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To anneal glass or metal is to heat and cool it slowly to toughen it, the same treatment as tempering.

clue.text: Cunning lies — wins by design

indicators.note: design here means arranging, so the letters of the two words are deliberately rearranged

explanation.surface: Cunning deceit succeeds through careful planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by design' signals that LIES and WINS are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cunning and craftiness are synonyms for the quality of being sly and full of tricks.

clue.text: Handle some rising shares in metal — up in a minute!

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
some means only part of the words is taken, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A trader handles shares in a metal that will go up any minute.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits backwards across 'metal — up in a minute', and 'rising' says to read it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle something skilfully, or a person deviously, is to manipulate them.

clue.text: Makes little of a respected doctor

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone belittles a highly regarded physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun, a respected physician, but works as the verb to tamper with, rearranging A RESPECTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate something is to disparage or play it down, belittling its worth.

clue.text: Girl providing cover for many soldiers

indicators.note: a cover is a disguise, so the word for the soldiers appears with its letters rearranged

parts.note: an army is a great body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A young woman shields a large force of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect anagram: 'cover', in the sense of disguise, rearranges ARMY, the word that 'many soldiers' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, and a girl's name is the usual crossword sense of girl.

clue.text: Precise value given to a small measure of uranium

parts.note: cc, a cubic centimetre, is a small measure
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
a rate is a value or price

explanation.surface: An exact price is set for a small amount of uranium.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and precise are synonyms meaning exact.

clue.text: In speech, recognises the narrow margin of victory

indicators.note: in speech means the word is heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: to know someone is to recognise them

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges how close the race was.
explanation.walkthrough: A horse that wins by the length of its snout has won by the smallest margin.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing results speak of winning by a short head or a snout's length, the smallest margin of victory.

clue.text: One of the signs of a tailless insect

indicators.note: tailless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the scorpion is loosely called an insect, though it is an arachnid

explanation.surface: Looking for signs of a bug that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' takes the last letter from SCORPION.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scorpion is the eighth sign of the zodiac, one of the twelve star signs.

clue.text: Magic broomstick?

definitions.meaning: the vehicle a sorceress rides, read as her aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: a broomstick is the craft, or vehicle, a witch flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is magic practised by witches; the broomstick is jokingly the flying vessel of a sorceress.

clue.text: A fragrance that's on the up?

parts.note: a scent is a pleasant smell, a fragrance

explanation.surface: A perfume that is becoming popular.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a climb, something going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb or upward movement is literally a thing on the up.

clue.text: Stars' groupie outside car

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as "Stars' groupie outside car" (6): MINI is the car, but no reading of 'groupie outside' gives GE around or before it; the clue looks garbled and no source was found.

clue.text: Discover London in bloom

parts.note: the Smoke, or Big Smoke, is a nickname for London
flowers that are out have opened

explanation.surface: Find the British capital full of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' is an old British nickname for London, from its coal fogs.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoke someone out is to drive them from hiding, so to discover them.

clue.text: Sister company admits one messenger

parts.note: a nun is called Sister

indicators.note: admits means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nun's business lets in a courier.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal envoy carries the Pope's messages to a foreign government, so he is a messenger.

clue.text: One almost expensive thought

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: dear means costly, expensive

explanation.surface: A single nearly costly notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' takes the last letter from DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought is a notion or concept in the mind.

clue.text: Carpet salesman runs admin badly

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put into the wrong order

explanation.surface: A rug seller manages the paperwork poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' looks like the seller's goods but is the verb to scold; 'badly' rearranges R and ADMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for calling them in to scold them, a telling-off.

clue.text: Relative who's very thin — not good!

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is left out of the word

parts.note: gaunt means very thin and bony

explanation.surface: A family member who is skin and bone is not well.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Grew rapidly in favour of long sentence merited

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a life sentence is the longest prison term
to rate is to deserve, so rated means merited

explanation.surface: Support for a deserved life term increased quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To proliferate is to multiply or spread quickly.
